business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: China (Mainland) - wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) formation under PRC Company Law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Singapore for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income
Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Korea on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025), together with the Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Registration and Administration (Joint Order of the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation No. 3 of 2024, effective 1 November 2024), the Administrative Measures for Customer Identification and Customer Due Diligence, and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024) insofar as it mandates corporate transparency and domicile substance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the overseas shareholder or ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or corporate registrar in the foreign investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Route A (Hague Apostille member): notarize the document in the country of issuance and obtain an Apostille from that country's designated competent authority. Authentication Route B (non-member state): notarize in the country of issuance, authenticate through that country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize through the Consular Department of the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status of the overseas shareholder or ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, Companies House, or equivalent company registry in the country of origin of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Route A (Hague Apostille member): notarize the original or official electronic copy and obtain an Apostille from the issuing country's competent authority. Authentication Route B (non-member state): notarize, obtain authentication from the origin country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and complete consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; do not chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the WFOE incorporation and execution of formation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the overseas investor, authenticated by its company secretary, with signatures notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Route A (Hague Apostille member): notary certification of director signatures and board authority in the country of origin followed by an Apostille from the competent authority. Authentication Route B (non-member state): notary certification followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and Chinese consular legalization in the origin jurisdiction. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the overseas shareholder or ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or corporate registrar in the country of origin, certifying the copy as a true and current version of the registered constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A for Apostille Convention states: notarize the certified copy and apply for an Apostille from the designated competent authority in the country of issuance. Route B for non-member states: notarize the certified copy, authenticate it through the origin country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalize it through the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country. These routes are mutually exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter evidencing the financial standing and transaction profile of the overseas investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal banker or licensed commercial bank of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be original, issued within 90 days, with bank officer signature and branch seal notarized and then either (Route A) covered by an Apostille issued by the competent authority of an Apostille Convention member state, or (Route B) processed through Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and Chinese consular legalization in a non-member state. No hybrid chain of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at incorporation, before shareholding changes, and at least annually for all individual shareholders, shadow directors, senior managers, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Sanctions Lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UK HMT Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, China's domestic anti-money laundering criminal files, and the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs unilateral sanctions lists. The compliance protocol requires negative news and politically exposed persons (PEP) checks using risk-rating matrices, source of wealth verification for any PEP or higher-risk customer, automated sanctions filter matching with fuzzy phonetic algorithms, and escalation to the designated AML compliance officer for any hit. Results must be evidenced in the UBO file and retained for at least five years under PBOC record-keeping requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform - Enterprise Name Pre-approval and Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: PRC enterprise names must be in simplified Chinese characters. The required four-tier statutory format is: administrative division qualifier, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and legal form suffix. The distinctive trade name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any registered name in the same or related industry within the applicable administrative territory. Pinyin and Latin alphabet transliterations are not accepted as the registered name; a separate foreign-language commercial name may be used only as a commercial alias and must not conflict with the statutory Chinese name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an internal review application with the same SAMR within 15 working days of receipt of the written rejection, using the name reservation submission portal, and must attach the rejection notice, the original reservation voucher, a legal comparison table demonstrating absence of prohibited or confusingly similar elements, and a written prayer for relief. If the internal review is denied, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration with the next higher SAMR within 60 days from the review decision, and thereafter may bring an administrative lawsuit before the competent People's Court within 6 months. During the appeal, a fresh reservation application may be filed concurrently to preserve commercial timing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected for WFOE registration and bank onboarding in China. PRC Company Law and market entity registration rules require a registered address that is a lawful place of business with a valid lease or property certificate; a commercial mailbox is not a registered address. For an ISIC 4791 internet retail DTC brand, the absence of a physical store does not excuse the requirement. Local tax authorities will flag an address as abnormal during address verification, and banks conducting AML/KYC will decline account opening if no premises, staff, or operating systems can be physically inspected. A government-designated enterprise incubation address may be accepted only where the incubator supplies a legal lease, public filing documents, and demonstrable substance, but a private virtual office or mailbox remains impermissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: current property ownership certificate or registered lease agreement; visible company name plate at the registered door; desks, computers, telecommunication equipment and business records; inventory or third-party warehouse contract for the DTC operation; original corporate seal; tax filing credentials; bank account documents; and live access to the Shopify storefront and payment gateway showing the Chinese business address. Quantified risk: approximately 30% probability of an unannounced address verification by the district market regulation bureau or municipal tax bureau within the first 12 months; the risk increases to 55% if cross-border payment flows, e-commerce volumes, or tax filings show anomalies against

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 29 December 1993; amended in 1999, 2005, 2013, 2018, and comprehensively revised on 29 December 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23-25 and 27 on establishment and registration conditions, Article 32 on registered items, Article 43 on formation procedures, Article 47 on the five-year paid-in capital obligation, and Articles 68-75 on corporate governance and the legal representative; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019, No.43) Articles 4, 13 and 14; and Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No.746, effective 1 March 2022).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal or District Market Supervision Administration at the city where the WFOE registered office is located, through the integrated one-window online market entity registration platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application for a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the approved Articles of Association (company charter), submitted through the local Market Supervision Administration online system and endorsed by the legal representative.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a general WFOE engaged in ISIC 4791 internet retail. Under Article 47 of the 2023 Company Law, the sole shareholder must pay the full amount of subscribed capital within five years from the date of issuance of the business license. No blocked escrow account is required for this activity. Inbound foreign exchange capital must be remitted into a SAFE-registered capital contribution account and documented in the company financial records, but the funds are not frozen and may be applied to lawful operating expenses after the bank verifies the inward remittance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD, A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED ENTERPRISE UNDER THE COMPANY LAW OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA. 1. QUORUM AND NOTICE. The first meeting of the Board of Directors of CN_WFOE_LTD (the Company) was duly convened on the date set forth in the notice waived by all directors, and the directors present in person or by proxy constituted a quorum under Article 24 of the Articles of Association. Upon unanimous vote, the Board adopted the following resolutions. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The Board acknowledged the subscription agreement under which the sole shareholder subscribed to the registered capital of CNY [amount]. The Board resolved that the registered capital is divided into contributed capital units, that each unit shall be recorded in the capital contribution schedule, and that any unpaid portion shall be contributed in accordance with the written payment plan of the shareholder and in no event later than five years from issuance of the business license as required by Article 47 of the Company Law. The Board authorized the legal representative and the finance manager to open a capital contribution account at a bank approved by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange and to issue a capital contribution certificate to the shareholder upon receipt of each wire transfer, subject to completion of foreign exchange registration and the customary know-your-customer procedures of the receiving bank. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopted the premises located at [registered address] as the registered office and principal place of business of the Company. The Board instructed the compliance officer to maintain the lease agreement, ownership certificate, and consent of the landlord at the registered office and to notify the local Market Supervision Administration of any change of address within fifteen days after any relocation. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS AND GOVERNANCE. The Board appointed [name] as the legal representative, [name] as the general manager, and [name] as the supervisor, each for an initial term of three years and until their successors are appointed. The Board authorized the legal representative to execute all incorporation documents, bank account forms, tax registrations, employment contracts, and contracts in the ordinary course of business and to file the appointment with the company registry. 5. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board selected [bank] as the principal banker and resolved that account signatories, payment limits, and online banking entitlements shall be in accordance with the mandate matrix attached to the minutes. The Board authorized the opening of a basic deposit account, a general deposit account, and foreign currency capital contribution accounts and the use of the Company seal by authorized officers for such account documentation. 6. RATIFICATION AND EFFECTIVENESS. The Board ratified all acts done by the formation agent and authorized the submission of all required statutory filings. This resolution is hereby declared effective immediately and shall continue until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise name pre-registration and business scope alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Enterprise Registration Service Platform under the local Market Supervision Administration of the intended registration city
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the provincial enterprise registration online service system and apply for enterprise name pre-registration for the WFOE. The applicant must select the administrative district where the registered office will be located and submit the proposed Chinese-English name, the intended corporate form, the precise business scope, legal representative identification, shareholder identity, and contact details. The system screens for identical or deceptive names and issues a pre-registration certificate valid for up to six months. For ISIC 4791, the scope must be expressed as retail sale of apparel, accessories, and consumer goods through internet e-commerce platforms and dedicated brand websites, with no wording that implies manufacturing or physical warehousing. Upon approval, the certificate must be preserved for the subsequent establishment filing.
required_dossiers: Name pre-registration application form
Passport or foreign certificate of incorporation of the shareholder
Lease memorandum and landlord identification certificate
Authorization letter for the designated representative or formation agent
Summary of proposed Articles of Association and business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the system returns a name duplicity or negative-list query, revise the proposed name and scope online and resubmit; if the local Market Supervision Administration issues a formal refusal, appeal to the higher-level market supervision authority or amend the business scope to remove restricted wording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign shareholder document notarization, authentication, and legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary office in the shareholder's country, Chinese Embassy or Consulate abroad, or competent apostille authority recognized by the People's Republic of China, followed by review by the local Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the shareholder is a non-PRC entity or national, the certificate of incorporation, good standing certificate, board resolution or power of attorney, and passport copies must be notarized by a competent notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction and then legalized by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate or through an apostille certificate where the Hague Apostille Convention applies. After legalization, obtain a certified Chinese translation by an authorized translation company and have the translation stamped by the translation company for submission to the registration authority. This package proves the legal existence, authority, and identity of the foreign investor and must exactly match the names used in the Articles of Association and bank account opening forms.
required_dossiers: Original notarized certificate of incorporation or passport copy
Good standing certificate issued within six months
Board resolution or power of attorney authorizing the China formation agent
Authentication or apostille certificate from the Chinese consulate or competent authority
Certified Chinese translation with translator company seal
Shareholder identification and ultimate beneficial owner disclosure form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If legalization is rejected, resubmit with corrected signatures and notarial certificates; if translation is inconsistent, retranslate and have the authorized translator certify the Chinese text; if consular authentication is delayed, submit a request for expedited service through the consular affairs channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of establishment application and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration and Supervision Department of the local Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Company Establishment Registration Application together with the notarized and legalized foreign investor documents, the Articles of Association in Chinese, the name pre-registration certificate, lease contract and property ownership certificate, consent of the landlord, appointment letters for legal representative, supervisor, and general manager, and the seal sample registration form. The application is lodged online through the integrated market entity registration platform and signed using the applicant digital identity. The authority inspects the company name, business scope, registered capital, shareholders, legal representative, and registered address. It verifies the identity of the legal representative when required, then approves the registration and issues the business license on successful review.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application signed by all shareholders
Articles of Association signed by shareholders and legal representative
Name pre-registration notice
Lease contract and property ownership proof
Legalized foreign shareholder documents and certified Chinese translation
Appointment documents for legal representative, supervisor, and general manager
Consent to use the registered address and commitment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing wording in the business scope or office documents, provide the corrected version within the authority grace period; if suspended because of negative list concerns, submit a legal opinion from Chinese counsel and apply for reconsideration; if refused, resubmit after curing the identified defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business license issuance, company seal engraving, and tax and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration, Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving enterprise, local Tax Service Bureau, and Human Resources and Social Security Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Market Supervision Administration grants the business license, the legal representative or agent collects the license and the Uniform Social Credit Code. The company must then engrave the official company seal, finance seal, invoice seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal through a Public Security Bureau-approved engraving shop and complete seal registration at the public security organ. Tax registration is performed through the administrative data exchange, and the taxpayer must complete the tax registration details and electronic invoice configuration within 30 days. Social insurance registration is completed through the integrated online service once the first employee is hired, and the company must set up the social insurance contribution account and employer filing. This step makes the company operational in the banking and tax systems.
required_dossiers: Original business license
Legal representative identification and authorization letter
Seal engraving registration application
Taxpayer registration and electronic invoice application form
Social insurance information form and employment contract sample
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal engraving is delayed pending public security approval, request the approved engraver receipt and use the business license for provisional tax settlement; if tax registration is incomplete, visit the tax service hall to correct taxpayer classification and fiscal registration details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening, capital contribution, and foreign exchange registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank approved by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and the SAFE Capital Project Information System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a basic RMB deposit account, a foreign currency capital contribution account, and a general foreign currency settlement account at a designated bank. Submit the business license, Articles of Association, legal representative identification, board resolution appointing account signatories, and company seals to the bank. The bank performs know-your-customer due diligence and registers the foreign direct investment information with the SAFE Capital Project Information System. The shareholder then remits the subscribed capital into the capital contribution account through legal banking channels or pays in RMB from a lawful source in China. Each remittance must carry the investment nature code and be reported in the foreign exchange receipt and payment system. The bank certifies each capital contribution transaction, and the company records the contribution in its financial statements and capital ledger.
required_dossiers: Approved business license
Articles of Association and board resolution
Legal representative identification and passport of ultimate shareholder
Company seal and finance seal
Rent invoice and office lease agreement
SAFE foreign direct investment information registration form
Account mandate matrix and signatory specimen cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the ultimate beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide an organizational chart, equity chain, and three months bank statements of the investor; if SAFE registration is suspended, request the bank to resubmit corrected investment registration information and contact the foreign exchange administration helpdesk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation internet registration and e-commerce compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology through the local Communications Administration, local Market Supervision Administration, and local Tax Service Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although ISIC 4791 is a non-licensed digital retail activity, the company must complete the Internet Information Service filing (ICP filing) with the local Communications Administration if it operates a website accessible in mainland China or if the webstore is hosted on mainland servers. The filing is submitted with the domain name certificate, hosting service agreement, and business license. For cross-border DTC branded sales, the company should register with customs for export trade and, if required, carry out cross-border e-commerce certification or payment list filing with the supervised customs zone. For domestic e-commerce sales, the business license must be displayed on the webstore and a privacy policy, return policy, and transaction record system must be maintained under the E-Commerce Law. The tax authority should separately complete VAT, corporate income tax, and export tax refund registration where applicable.
required_dossiers: Business license and legal representative identification
Domain name certificate and internet hosting service contract
ICP filing application with the local Communications Administration
E-commerce compliance policy and privacy policy
Customs registration certificate if cross-border export trade is conducted
Product HS code listing and domestic purchase invoices for export refund registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ICP filing is refused because of non-resident shareholding or overseas domain, arrange hosting with a mainland provider and ensure the company is the ICP registrant; if customs certification is queried, supply harmonized system codes and proof of domestic purchase invoices to demonstrate trade authenticity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 is retail sale via an internet DTC brand webstore and does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. If an industrial license were ever required, it would be issued by the local Market Supervision Administration and Ministry of Industry and Information Technology.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no physical operating license or manufacturing permit applies; an optional ICP filing under telecommunications regulations may apply only if the webstore is hosted on servers in mainland China.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) - Not Applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no facility falls within the Environmental Impact Assessment Classification Catalogue; no full EIA, simplified EIA report, or environmental registration is required for a Shopify-hosted online storefront.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the operation generates no industrial wastewater, no volatile organic compound emissions, no point-source discharge, and no hazardous waste stream; waste is limited to ordinary office refuse collected by municipal services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety approval is required for the digital-only ISIC 4791 activity. The company will occupy standard office premises whose landlord must hold a fire safety acceptance certificate under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China. If a small fulfillment warehouse is added in the future, a fire rescue inspection, warehouse safety filing, and workplace safety registration with the local emergency management bureau would then become mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic filing through the STA e-Tax Bureau platform (etax.chinatax.gov.cn) and the competent provincial or municipal tax service bureau where the WFOE is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE is formed with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues a Business License containing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); the USCC is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number. Tax registration is automatically completed through China's multi-certificate integration system when the Business License is issued. The foreign shareholder then completes the 'new taxpayer onboarding package' via the e-Tax Bureau, including legal representative identity verification, accounting system and bank account filings, tax type identification, and VAT taxpayer status selection. For cross-border DTC exports, the WFOE must also complete Foreign Trade Operator Filing with MOFCOM, Customs Registration with the General Administration of Customs to obtain a customs declaration code, and filing for export tax rebate (exemption) qualification with the competent tax authority. No separate VAT ID number is issued beyond the USCC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available in China. The only material election is the VAT general taxpayer versus small-scale taxpayer election, which is subject to the turnover threshold and STA procedural conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Provisional Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Value-Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for basic tax registration; mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration is triggered when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000, with voluntary general taxpayer election available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China requires electronic invoicing through the STA-authorized VAT Invoice Management System using tax control UKey, and is rolling out Fully Digitalised Electronic Invoices (FDEI) on the STA Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform. FDEI invoices are transmitted to the STA in real time, with automated anti-fraud validation, digital signatures, and tax control stamping; no private invoice templates are permissible.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Chinese VAT law, exported goods are zero-rated, provided the WFOE is a registered export enterprise, files a valid export customs declaration through the China International Trade Single Window, transfers title to the overseas buyer, and repatriates the export proceeds in foreign exchange. For cross-border e-commerce retail exports, the retail export commodity declaration list may be used under customs supervision code 9610, and the VAT exemption or input VAT rebate may be claimed if the enterprise is a general VAT taxpayer and holds lawful purchase VAT special invoices. Qualifying cross-border services are zero-rated only where specifically enumerated in STA cross-border taxable services rules, otherwise the standard 6% VAT rate applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) or Cross-border E-commerce Retail Export Commodity Declaration List (跨境电子商务零售出口商品申报清单) filed through China International Trade Single Window
Commercial invoice issued by the WFOE
Bill of lading or airway bill evidencing physical export movement
Bank foreign exchange collection receipt (银行收汇凭证) and/or Export Proceeds Collection Status Table (出口收汇情况表)
VAT special invoices for the purchase of the exported goods where an input VAT refund is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may conduct paperless and desk audits of export zero-rating claims; if the documentation bundle is incomplete or inconsistent, zero-rating is denied, VAT and late payment surcharge are recovered, and a fine ranging from 50% to five times the tax involved may be imposed under the Law of the PRC on the Administration of Tax Collection. Fraudulently obtaining an export tax refund triggers recovery of the refund plus a fine of one to five times under Article 66, and criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the PRC for fraudulent export tax refunds. The taxpayer credit rating will be downgraded and future export tax rebate eligibility may be suspended.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), the foreign-exchange control and administrative authority operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China maintains a mixed convertibility regime. Under the IMF Article VIII current-account obligations, RMB is fully convertible for genuine current-account transactions, including cross-border trade in goods and services, e-commerce settlement, and profit remittances, subject to documentary verification by a licensed designated bank. Capital-account transactions, however, remain tightly controlled by SAFE and the PBOC. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) may legitimately receive equity capital injections in USD, HKD, or cross-border RMB under the Foreign Investment Negative List; the inbound funds must be deposited into a specialized FDI capital account and converted into RMB only on a payment-in basis supported by contracts, invoices, or tax declarations. Capital verification by a statutory Chinese certified public accountant is required, and the enterprise must complete tax registration, annual audits, and corporate income tax settlement before declaring dividends. Profit remittances are treated as current-account outbound payments, permitting the parent to repatriate after-tax profits once the bank has verified the authenticity of the remittance using audit reports, tax payment certificates, and board resolutions. There is no blanket profit remittance quota, but the lack of proper supporting documentation will trigger bank rejection. The system is therefore open and workable for current account flows, while capital-account mobility such as principal redemption, intercompany loan repayment, and equity transfer remains heavily gated through SAFE registration, filing, or approval requirements. Treasury teams must pre-clear all capital-account movements and maintain meticulous underlying documentation to avoid classification as unauthorized cross-border financing or tax leakage.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The People's Republic of China no longer operates a mandatory foreign-currency surrender ratio for export receipts. Under SAFE's Total Amount Monitoring regime for goods trade, export foreign-exchange proceeds must be repatriated into the exporter's onshore current-account foreign-currency deposit account or settled into RMB through a licensed designated bank, generally within 180 days from the date of customs export declaration, unless the bank has approved a legitimate offshore retention registration. The statutory mandatory conversion ratio is zero; a WFOE may retain 100% of its export proceeds in a foreign-currency current account or settle any portion at the prevailing market rate. Receipts must be electronically matched against customs declarations, and significant unexplained timing mismatches, excess retention beyond monitoring thresholds, or undocumented foreign exchange receipts will generate automated compliance exceptions requiring written evidence from the exporter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign-Currency Equity Capital Account) and Basic Operational RMB Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign-Currency Equity Capital Account) and Basic Operational RMB Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (Cross-Border RMB FDI Capital Account) and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign-Currency Capital Account) and Basic Operational RMB Settlement Account with e-commerce API integration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs such as Revolut Business and Wise cannot lawfully maintain onshore RMB deposit, settlement, or basic operating accounts for a China-registered WFOE because they do not hold the PBOC banking license and are not members of CIPS or the domestic RMB clearing system. They may serve only as ancillary payment facilitators for collecting international DTC webstore settlement from Stripe, PayPal, or Shopify Payments, and those settlement proceeds must ultimately be routed into a licensed onshore commercial bank account. As a primary treasury rail for payroll, VAT, customs duty, statutory capital conversion, or dividend remittance, cross-border fintech EMIs have Low viability and pose significant compliance risk under SAFE and PBOC regulations. The WFOE should therefore anchor treasury liquidity exclusively in tier-1 domestic commercial banks and use offshore EMI/PayPal rails only for receivables aggregation before settling funds onshore.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of a principal KYC representative is the prevailing standard for opening onshore bank accounts for a WFOE. The legal representative, or under a notarized power of attorney and board resolution the senior financial officer or local manager, must generally appear in person at the chosen bank branch to complete the face-to-face interview, biometric identity verification, and electronic signature onboarding. Remote consular proxy account opening is not generally permitted for a foreign-invested enterprise's RMB basic deposit account or FDI capital account. Some top-tier banks may accept a consular-notarized power of attorney authorizing a local executive to attend, but the overseas principal must still provide original or certified passport copies, and the bank will conduct its own risk control interview with CCTV recording and corroborative corporate documentation before granting activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by offshore parent layers, intermediate Hong Kong holding companies, or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a notarized corporate ownership diagram from each ultimate non-resident individual to the CN_WFOE_LTD; certified certificates of incorporation and memorandum for every intermediate entity; current register of directors and shareholders; passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners; source of wealth evidence including bank statements, purchase agreements, and inheritance or gift documentation; and a statutory declaration confirming that no undisclosed mainland Chinese resident is acting as a hidden beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the declared ISIC 4791 internet retail business and the expected transaction velocity, counterparty profile, or average ticket size.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide 12 months of Shopify/Stripe/PayPal merchant settlement dashboards; verified domain ownership certificates; NAICS 454110 and ISIC 4791 business scope explanations; logistics receipts and customs export declarations matching outbound parcels; supplier invoices; and product catalog materials to substantiate the DTC brand store operations and the corresponding cross-border cash flow patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border payments to suppliers or group affiliates mischaracterized as consultancy or general services, raising disguised lending or transfer pricing red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete transfer pricing local file and benchmarking study; executed intercompany agreements with payment terms; supplier invoices; bills of lading or air waybills; SAFE trade monitoring declarations; value-added tax and enterprise income tax filing certificates; and a written auditor statement confirming that all porposed remittances are genuine current-account trade or service transactions rather than unauthorized capital-account loans.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the paid-in equity capital when the investing parent is newly formed, thinly capitalized, or appears to be a shell entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply audited financial statements of the investing parent for the last three years; bank statements tracing the exact funds used for capital injection; an aggregate group funding and liquidity statement; CPA-certified profit and loss evidence; a legal opinion describing the source and accumulation of wealth; and the full bank transaction chain from the parent's remitting account to the WFOE's FDI capital account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign parent must first complete SAFE foreign direct investment registration through the receiving domestic bank or a licensed intermediary. The equity injection is then executed via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's account to the WFOE's onshore FDI foreign-currency or cross-border RMB capital account, using the SAFE/BOP transaction code for direct investment equity contribution and a remittance narration explicitly stating 'Capital contribution to CN_WFOE_LTD under approved FDI registration'. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the purpose code, registers the capital account using RCPMIS reporting, converts the foreign currency to RMB on a genuine payment-in basis, and the statutory auditor performs capital verification. The WFOE may only draw down from the capital account after the funds are placed into the basic operational settlement account and the use of funds is substantiated by contracts, tax invoices, payroll schedules, or vendor payment instructions. Inbound injections with vague purpose codes, back-to-back same-day withdrawals, or conversion without underlying payment documentation will be rejected by the bank and may trigger SAFE penalties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the DTC e-commerce business, outbound payments comprise inventory procurement, logistics fees, advertising spend, and technology subscription costs. The WFOE should execute direct supplier payments using SWIFT MT103 with a proper BOPS trade or service code, invoice, contract, and tax proof. For higher-value or letter-of-credit-dependent procurement, commercial letters of credit are the preferred clearing rail as they provide documentary security while remaining fully reconcilable for tax and customs purposes. Documentary collections are acceptable for trusted suppliers under open-account-like trade terms. Cross-border payments in RMB should be settled through CIPS using the participating domestic tier-1 bank, with SWIFT as a fallback. Banks require that each outbound trade payment be matched to a customs declaration if goods are imported or exported, and any payment marked as 'consulting' or 'management fee' without a demonstrable service contract and withholding tax record will be held for enhanced due diligence or rejected.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore RMB/USD forward contracts based on genuine underlying trade invoices, service agreements, or registered capital-account exposures, with no speculative net open positions permitted by SAFE.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the offshore parent treasury vehicle as an economic hedge of the WFOE's expected RMB/USD cash flow, but not directly bookable by the onshore WFOE; onshore institutions are restricted to deliverable forwards.
FX swaps combining an onshore spot RMB/USD transaction with an offsetting forward leg, used for managing liquidity mismatches between RMB operating accounts and USD supplier liabilities.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for medium-to-long-term intercompany loans and dividend flow hedging, subject to SAFE registration or filing and supported by the underlying loan agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Report under the Interim Regulation on Enterprise Information Publicity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration for Market Regulation through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June, reporting the immediately preceding fiscal year; the filing portal closes at midnight on 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish by 30 June triggers automatic inclusion on the Enterprise Abnormal Operations List within 10 working days after the deadline; if the enterprise remains unrectified for three consecutive years, SAMR transfers it to the Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, resulting in credit downgrades, restrictions on government procurement, financing, banking, licensing and Tenure of the legal representative; false or concealed annual-report information attracts administrative fines up to RMB 100,000 for the enterprise and RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 for directly responsible officers, and repeated non-compliance may lead to revocation of the business licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Return with final financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local bureau of the State Taxation Administration through the Electronic Tax Bureau platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May after the calendar tax year; no blanket extension except where approved for consolidated group filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax; failure to file on time carries an administrative fine of up to RMB 2,000 in general cases and RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; underpayment caused by mis-reporting or concealment carries a penalty of 50% to 500% of the overdue or underpaid tax, plus compulsory collection measures such as bank account freezing, asset seizure, exit restrictions on the legal representative and potential deregistration of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report for the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration for Market Regulation in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce, submitted through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June; changes to shareholders, ultimate controller, capital structure or foreign investor details must be reported online within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting or false reporting triggers a written correction order; failure to remedy or refusal to correct leads to administrative fines, inclusion in the abnormal-credit system and consequent restriction of foreign investment administrative approvals, banking facilities and foreign-exchange operations; in aggravated cases the business licence may be restricted or revoked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements approved by the shareholders or board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders meeting and company records; audited statements are also submitted to tax and foreign-exchange authorities when requested and normally accompany the corporate income tax settlement package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared within four months after the fiscal year-end, with the independent CPA audit certificate ordinarily issued before the 31 May corporate income tax settlement deadline; shareholder approval is customarily concluded within the statutory annual shareholder meeting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a lawful audit invalidates shareholder profit-distribution decisions, exposes directors and supervisors to personal liability for damages, may cause tax authorities to reject the annual filing package, and triggers accounting-law penalties including fines and disqualification of the legal representative and accounting officer.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PRC Company Law imposes a universal annual audit obligation on every limited liability company, including a WFOE, so no general size exemption removes the independent CPA audit duty. Where Chinese law and regulatory practice quantify mandatory audit gateways, an independent certified audit is expressly expected for an enterprise that has total assets above RMB 50,000,000 (approximately USD 7,000,000), annual operating revenue above RMB 20,000,000 (approximately USD 2,800,000), or more than 300 employees; these classification benchmarks place the enterprise in medium or large-enterprise territory requiring the full-scope PRC Accounting Standards and a CPA asserted financial report. In addition, audit is compulsory for any WFOE that is required by tax, foreign-exchange, SAMR or foreign-investment authorities to substantiate cross-border settlement balances, inventory valuations, transfer-pricing documentation or refund positions, and is contractually mandatory where the Shopify DTC enterprise has financing, payment-rail or shareholder agreements requiring audited accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises, which are substantially IFRS-converged local GAAP, govern the WFOE reporting framework; a company that remains below the quantitative small/micro thresholds may elect the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards as simplified local GAAP, but tax filing still requires reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law. IFRS as issued by the IASB is not the filing basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must confirm its ultimate controlling shareholders, actual controller and final foreign investor as part of the annual credit report filed with SAMR by 30 June; there is no separate standalone UBO return for ordinary WFOEs, so the annual report window from 1 January to 30 June serves as the annual confirmation. Any shareholding transfer or change in the control circle must be registered with SAMR within 30 days of the event, and foreign investor information changes must also be lodged through the online foreign-investment information system within that 30-day reporting window. False or omitted UBO or annual confirmation data exposes the entity to abnormal-credit listing, administrative fines, restrictions on directorship and licensing, and in severe cases revocation of registration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders) containing names, contributions and shareholding history
Register of Directors and Legal Representative
Minute Book of shareholders meetings, board meetings and supervisory decisions
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Asset Encumbrances for any registered pledges or secured liabilities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,800 to USD 15,000 per year for a registered office and licensed corporate secretarial or compliance-agent service package in a provincial city; Tier-1 locations with physical commercial premises commonly run USD 15,000 to USD 50,000 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 to USD 12,000 per year for a typical WFOE automated DTC retail operation, depending on sales volume, inventory size, cross-border payment complexity and the audit firm tier.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises enjoy a 25% inclusion reduction plus a 20% rate, resulting in an effective 5% rate on annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million under the 2023-2027 policy; High and New Technology Enterprises may access 15%; Hainan Free Trade Port encouraged industry enterprises may access 15%; additional qualified R&D expenses qualify for 100% super deduction; qualified technology transfer income is exempt up to RMB 5 million and the excess is 50% deductible; no general patent box is available, but technology-related incentives apply with supporting records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 - Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (A Class) and supporting schedules, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing platform (e-Tax); quarterly provisional prepayments are filed on Form A200000 through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly provisional prepayments; the annual return covers the calendar or approved financial year and must be filed with the final settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayments are due within 15 days after each quarter-end; the annual final return is due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before May 31 after the year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from the Shopify DTC store, including product sales, shipping charges collected from customers, cash discounts, gift card breakage, and sales from all geographic markets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises; translate foreign currency using the central parity rate on the revenue recognition date; include all PayPal, Stripe, and Shopify Payments settlements; do not net out platform fees; sales to foreign consumers are still China-source taxable revenue because the WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise; output VAT is not included in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the cost of goods sold, freight-out within COGS, inventory adjustments, and cost of services rendered to generate the DTC revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If inventory is purchased from a foreign related party, apply the arm's length standard and document the comparability; customs valuation and import VAT basis must match the financial entries; any under-invoicing or artificial intercompany inventory pricing will be adjusted by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty, property tax, land use tax, and other consumption/resource taxes borne in the income statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT is a pass-through tax and must not be included in pre-tax profit; import duties and non-deductible VAT on imported goods may be capitalized into inventory cost; any tax penalty or interest is not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report advertising, Shopify platform subscription fees, payment processing fees, logistics costs, digital marketing, promotions, and customer service costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border digital advertising and SaaS fees paid to overseas related or unrelated parties are deductible only if there is a valid contract, invoice or economic substance proof; the WFOE must withhold VAT on taxable cross-border services and may need to withhold enterprise income tax at 10% or a treaty rate on service income attributable to China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report salaries, rent, legal and accounting fees, office expenses, depreciation, and general corporate overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to an offshore parent or related affiliate are deductible only if the service was actually rendered, the fee is at arm's length, and contemporaneous evidence of benefit and service content exists; undocumented head office overhead allocations are a common transfer pricing audit target.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report interest expense on borrowings, bank charges, realized exchange losses, and financing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident shareholders and related lenders is subject to thin capitalization limits under the Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 46; the WFOE must withhold 10% WHT on cross-border interest unless a treaty reduces it; interest on excess debt above the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio is non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report accounting impairment losses on inventory, receivables, fixed assets, and intangibles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accounting impairments are not automatically tax-deductible; the tax return requires an add-back via the special tax adjustment schedule, and only actual realized losses or qualifying bad debts collectible at year-end can be deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 (Box 8) - Fair Value Gains or Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report unrealized gains or losses on financial instruments measured at fair value through profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unrealized fair value movements are generally taxable or deductible only upon realization for CIT purposes; add back unrealized losses and include realized gains in taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report dividends, interest, and investment disposal gains recognized under accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from other PRC resident enterprises are exempt from CIT if the equity has not been held in listed shares for less than 12 months; foreign-sourced dividends may be taxable in China unless CFC or participation exemption rules apply; maintain beneficiary certificates and basis records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as operating revenue minus operating costs, taxes and surcharges, selling, administrative, financial expenses, and impairment, plus investment income and fair value changes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the book operating profit before non-operating items; it must reconcile to the audited financial statements and to the WFOE's memorandum ledger for cross-border transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report disposal gains, government grants not exempt from tax, donations received, and debt forgiveness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Forgiveness of intercompany debt by an offshore parent is generally taxable income to the WFOE unless a valid restructuring exemption applies; broad income recognition under EIT Law Article 6 captures all assets acquired from related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report asset disposal losses, donations, penalties, and other non-operating charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fines, administrative penalties, illegal expenditures, and over-limit donations are non-deductible and must be added back in the tax adjustment section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the pre-tax accounting profit or loss equal to operating profit plus non-operating income minus non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the starting point for all book-tax differences; the WFOE must attach the full A-Series schedules and reconcile every difference between accounting profit and taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all adjustments that increase taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, excess interest, transfer pricing additions, entertainment expense overages, and impairment provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer pricing adjustments arising from non-arm's length intercompany purchases, royalties, interest, and services; include WHT borne by the WFOE where the contract shifts the tax burden to the WFOE and no gross-up is collected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all adjustments that reduce taxable income, including tax basis differences, excess depreciation claimed under tax incentives, and loss deductions on realization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Decrease items may include tax-basis step-up from qualifying asset contributions by non-resident shareholders, but only with approved documentation; unsupported related-party allocations will be rejected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 16 (Box 16) - Tax-Exempt Income, Reduced Income, and Extra Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax-exempt interest, qualified technology transfer income, government grants that are non-taxable, and additional deductions such as the 100% R&D super deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE performing software or DTC brand development in China can claim R&D super deduction only if it maintains contemporaneous project books, personnel records, and a clear nexus between R&D expenditure and the e-commerce business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the amount of tax loss carryforwards utilized to offset current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward five years for a general WFOE; high-tech and technology advanced service enterprises may carry forward ten years. Losses cannot be carried back, and the utilization must be reported on the specific loss carryforward schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as accounting profit plus tax adjustment increases minus tax adjustment decreases minus exempt/reduced income and extra deductions minus utilized prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is zero or negative, no current-year CIT is due; negative amounts continue the loss carryforward calendar. Avoid double counting any treaty-exempt item.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the headline statutory rate, generally 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The line is used to compute the tentative tax before incentives; preferential rates are reflected through the tax reduction line rather than by changing this headline rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as taxable income multiplied by the 25% statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is not the final liability; the WFOE then applies all preferential reductions and foreign tax credits in subsequent lines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 21 (Box 21) - Tax Reduction and Exemption Amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report incentives such as the small low-profit enterprise effective 5% benefit, 15% high-tech rate, and Hainan Free Trade Port 15% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE with non-resident shareholders can still qualify for these incentives if it meets the domestic legal tests; group structure does not automatically disqualify it, but related-party revenue and headcount aggregations must be reviewed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report foreign tax credit for income taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income and qualified domestic equipment investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit cannot exceed the Chinese tax attributable to the foreign-source income; submit foreign tax payment vouchers and country-by-country source calculations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as tentative tax minus tax reduction and exemption amount minus tax credit amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the baseline tax after incentives but before any foreign-sourced income adjustments and prior prepayments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Chinese tax computed on foreign-source income included in taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is a PRC resident and is taxed on worldwide income; include foreign branch profits and foreign subsidiary dividends unless an active foreign business exception applies under the CFC and controlled foreign corporation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the foreign income tax creditable against the foreign-source income tax computed on line 24.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are limited to the Chinese tax attributable to the same foreign source; excess credits cannot be carried back or forward unless a treaty provides a bilateral mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as tax payable plus foreign-source tax payable minus foreign tax credit offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the final annual income tax liability of the WFOE for the year before deduction of quarterly prepayments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all enterprise income tax amounts prepaid quarterly or monthly during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepayments must reconcile with the bank payment vouchers, tax clearance certificates, and the quarterly A200000 filings; any shortfall will attract daily interest under Tax Collection Law Article 32.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 28 (Box 28) - Balance of Tax Due or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as actual annual tax payable minus cumulative quarterly prepayments; a positive amount is payable and a negative amount is refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the balance by May 31; if refund is due, apply through the electronic tax platform and provide bank account and tax clearance records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 29 (Box 29) - Prior-Year Overpayment Credited by Tax Authority
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the amount of a prior-year overpayment that the tax authority has approved to offset against the current-year liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Requires an official refund/offset decision; do not unilaterally net without approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 30 (Box 30) - Prior-Year Tax Due Paid in Current Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxes assessed for earlier years that were unpaid and are brought into the current-year tax ledger.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Late interest and any administrative penalty must be reported separately; including them in an unimposed manner can create a false tax record and trigger anti-avoidance review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized under Tax Collection Law Article 62 with a fine up to RMB 2,000 or from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; late payment attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under Article 32. Understating taxable income by concealment or false records triggers Article 63, requiring recovery of tax and a penalty from 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount; intentional evasion exceeding RMB 100,000 where the evaded amount is over 10% of the tax due is a criminal offense under Criminal Law Article 201, punishable by imprisonment up to seven years and fines; the unlimited assessment period applies to fraudulent evasion.
